claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Since Alex is between 16-19 years old, eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training, or if they recently left such a course. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's education or training situation. For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit can continue if they're in approved education or training, or in some cases, for a short period after they've left.

**Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **Currently in education or training** - Alex is enrolled in and attending an approved course
2. **Recently left education or training** - Alex has left education/training within the last 20 weeks
3. **Neither** - Alex is not in education/training and it's been more than 20 weeks since leaving, or never enrolled

Which situation describes Alex?

conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about Alex's education situation at the moment. I don't know if they're in any kind of course or training right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay! Let me ask a few clarifying questions to help determine Alex's situation:

**Is Alex currently enrolled in any of the following?**

- A college or sixth form course (like A-levels, BTECs, etc.)
- An apprenticeship or vocational training program
- Any other educational course or training
- Not enrolled in anything at the moment

If Alex isn't currently in education or training, do you know:
- **When did Alex last finish school or leave any course?** (This helps us determine if they might be within the 20-week extension period)

These details will help me accurately assess eligibility. If you're genuinely unsure about Alex's current status, you might want to check with Alex directly, as this is a key factor in determining Child Benefit eligibility for 19-year-olds.

What can you tell me about Alex's current situation?

I understand - you don't have information about Alex's education or training status right now. This is actually crucial information for determining Child Benefit eligibility for a 19-year-old.

**Here's the situation:**

For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit eligibility depends entirely on whether they are:
- Currently enrolled in approved education or training (meeting specific criteria), OR
- Within 20 weeks of leaving approved education/training

Without knowing Alex's education status, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility.

**What I recommend:**

1. **Find out from Alex** whether they are:
   - Currently enrolled in any education or training course
   - If not, when they last left education or finished a course

2. **Once you have this information**, I can continue the assessment and give you a clear answer about eligibility

3. **Alternatively**, you could apply for Child Benefit and provide the information in your application - the Child Benefit Office will assess Alex's education status as part of processing your claim

Would you like to find out this information from Alex and come back to complete the assessment, or do you have any other questions I can help with in the meantime?

3. **If they're not currently enrolled:** When did they finish their last course or leave education?

Once you have this information, feel free to come back and we can continue the assessment. I'll be able to tell you definitively whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**In the meantime:**

If you'd like to start the application process, you can visit the official Child Benefit page at gov.uk, though having Alex's education details will make the process smoother.
